rules.description: Production is never brokered from this host. A deny-rule placed first cannot be reached around, because the first matching rule decides.

An exception, placed deliberately ABOVE the rule it carves a hole in. Because the first matching rule decides, this deny takes agent-quarantine out of the broader agent-* allow immediately below — while every other agent-* label still gets it. Order is the whole mechanism: move this rule below the next one and it never fires at all. `parzival policy validate` reports the overlap as a warning rather than an error precisely because this shape is normal — it cannot tell a deliberate exception from an accidental one, so it says what it sees and leaves the judgement to you.
Gitea token for AI agents and other non-human callers: brokered delivery only, so an agent can USE the credential without ever seeing its value.

Same ref, human and service identities, working hours only. Note this rule ALSO lists modes without get. That is what makes the rule above real: identity labels are self-asserted, so if any single rule permitted get on this ref, a caller could pass --as tea and read the raw value regardless of the agent restriction. Restrict the REF, not the IDENTITY. Verify with: parzival policy check

A deliberate raw-value exception: interactive human use of a personal vault, piped by hand to a tool with no other interface. `parzival policy check` reports this ref as readable, which is correct and expected here. Do not write a rule of this shape for any ref a non-human identity can reach.
